candidateDecisions.label: Medicine use, health behaviour & public health
Drug discovery, pharmaceutical chemistry & formulation
candidateDecisions.assessment: UCR has biochemistry and pharmacology but no cumulative chemistry, pharmaceutical analysis, dosage-form technology, biopharmaceutics, medicinal chemistry, organic synthesis, drug design or formulation-and-delivery sequence. A third programme would misrepresent general life-science and data courses as pharmaceutical development training.

stoppingDecision.assessment: Two complete related-fields programmes are defensible: one centred on molecular disease, pharmacology and biomedical evidence, and one centred on medicine use, health behaviour and patient context. The next generator-backed direction is drug discovery, chemistry and formulation; UCR cannot implement it, so production stops at two and preserves the specialist and professional gaps explicitly.

analysis: The closest option has a substantive foundation in physiology, cell biology, biochemistry and laboratory work, and extends it through pathophysiology, immunity and drug action. Pharmacology supports target and receptor analysis, pharmacokinetics and selected therapies. The lab contributes aseptic work, susceptibility testing and molecular methods, and statistical and data courses supply methods for evaluating evidence. The second option retains epidemiology, pharmacology, health psychology and evidence synthesis. It uses social psychology and qualitative methods for patient experience, ethical persuasion for communication methods, and public economics for health policy, equity and social insurance. Moving Behavioral Economics to the final autumn resolves the sole offering conflict. Adding Human Physiology, Mechanisms of Disease and Public Economics grounds the second option in treatment context and public health. Communication and leadership are complementary, not pharmacist training. A discovery or formulation option was tested against the current course descriptions and enriched topics. Biochemistry, the life-science laboratory and Pharmacology address enzymes, biomolecules, molecular methods, drug targets and kinetics. These do not form a cumulative sequence in chemical synthesis, pharmaceutical assays, formulation, dosage forms or drug delivery. Data science cannot supply that missing specialist progression. The two options satisfy the pairwise floor and teach distinct approaches, with different empirical and scientific methods. Comparator-only components preserve important clinical, technology, chemistry and research gaps.

Both study cells, membranes and molecular processes. Groningen continues the sequence in a second course.
Both study drug targets and receptor mechanisms. UCR Pharmacology also introduces pharmacokinetics and therapeutic examples.
Both study mechanisms of disease across human organ systems.
Both examine immune mechanisms and inflammation. Groningen studies these mechanisms in relation to medicines.
